answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the value it claims, like pigment layered until a forgery costs more than it gains. Peers attest real work and the stake earns yield; when two identities are proven to share one operator, both stakes are slashed. A sudden gale of new accounts then faces a real delta between cheap signup and expensive, slashable commitment, so farming a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, not one.
